bug_description.normalized: The staged 524-byte RAR5 witness reaches `process_block()` on a compressed block whose parsed header advertises `is_table_present`, so libarchive enters `parse_tables()` to expand the block's Huffman-table description. `parse_tables()` stores decoded bit lengths in local `uint8_t bit_length[HUFF_BC]` where `HUFF_BC == 20`. When a table nibble equals `ESCAPE` (15), the next nibble is interpreted as a run-length code: zero means literal 15, any nonzero value requests `value + 2` zero bytes. On the crashing iteration, the witness supplies an escape nibble followed by a nonzero nibble after earlier iterations have already advanced `w` near the end of `bit_length`. The vulnerable loop `for(k = 0; k < value + 2; k++) bit_length[w++] = 0;` never rechecks `w < HUFF_BC`, so it keeps writing after the 20-byte stack array is full. Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow WRITE 7` in `parse_tables`, matching the reported `parse_tables -> process_block -> do_uncompress_file` crash state. The fixing commit adds the missing `w < HUFF_BC` conjunct to the inner zero-fill loop.

source.description: First project-side parser statement on the crashing block that materializes vulnerability-relevant state from attacker-controlled bytes: it decodes the compressed-block header into `rar->last_block_hdr` and `block_size`, including the `is_table_present` flag that gates entry into `parse_tables()`.
source.value_from: Stage 01 reproduced the crash on the exact 524-byte `poc` RAR5 archive. On the crashing path, this call parses the current compressed-block header successfully, and the later branch at line 2824 proves that the decoded header set `rar->last_block_hdr.block_flags.is_table_present` for the same attacker-controlled block.

tainted_value_origin.description: On the escape path, `parse_tables()` reads the next attacker-controlled 4-bit code from the Huffman-table stream and uses it as the run-length base for the later `value + 2` zero-fill.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. The repeated zero-fill store overruns the 20-byte stack array `bit_length` when the escape-coded run continues after `w` reaches `HUFF_BC`.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow WRITE 7` in `parse_tables` at line 2028 and identifies `bit_length` as the frame object at line 1992 occupying `[32, 52)`, with the first invalid address exactly at offset 52.

root_cause.description: Root cause: the zero-fill expansion loop bounds only `k` against `value + 2` and omits any inner `w < HUFF_BC` check, so an escape-coded run near the end of `bit_length[20]` keeps writing past the stack buffer.
root_cause.note: The fixing patch changes this loop to `for(k = 0; (k < value + 2) && (w < HUFF_BC); k++)`, which is exactly the missing obligation in the vulnerable code.

parser_admitted.description: After the current compressed-block header is parsed and `process_block()` advances to the current block payload, the `is_table_present` bit routes execution into the Huffman-table parser instead of skipping directly to literal decoding.

coarse_trace.summary: Reading file data from the crafted RAR5 entry dispatches the compressed-data path, which drives `do_unpack()` into `uncompress_file()`.
The decompressor asks `process_block()` to parse the next compressed block before any output bytes are produced.
The current compressed-block header is parsed, its `is_table_present` bit is honored, and the staged block payload is passed into `parse_tables()`.
The Huffman-table parser expands escape-coded zero runs into local `bit_length[20]`; a nonzero escape run near the end of that array overruns the stack buffer.

fine_trace.note: This call parses the attacker-controlled compressed-block header and stores its fields in `rar->last_block_hdr`. On the crashing path, that parsed state includes a true `block_flags.is_table_present`, which is the control bit that makes `parse_tables()` run on this block.

The parsed block-header flag is true on the witness, so after `process_block()` finishes consuming the variable-size header it passes the current compressed-block payload pointer `p` directly into `parse_tables()` instead of skipping table parsing. This is the control decision that reaches the vulnerable code.

On the crashing `parse_tables()` iteration, the next 4-bit code read from the staged Huffman-table stream is `ESCAPE` (15). That steers execution away from the direct `bit_length[w++] = value` case and into the extended escape decoder.

Because step 3 read `ESCAPE`, the parser consumes the next 4-bit code from the same attacker-controlled stream as the escape payload. On the witness this second nibble is nonzero, so line 2019's `value == 0` literal-15 case is bypassed and the parser selects the zero-fill path.

Root cause. The nonzero escape payload is converted into a zero-run length of `value + 2`, but this inner loop checks only `k < value + 2`. Earlier outer-loop iterations have already advanced `w` close to `HUFF_BC == 20`, and the outer `for(w < HUFF_BC)` condition at line 2001 is not rechecked here. The fix adds the missing `w < HUFF_BC` conjunct to this loop.

Each iteration of step 5 executes this store into the 20-byte stack array `bit_length`. Once `w` reaches the end of the array, the same zero-fill loop keeps running because its guard still depends only on `k`. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting `stack-buffer-overflow WRITE 7` here and names `bit_length` as the overflown stack object at line 1992.

poc.trigger: Feeding the staged 524-byte `poc` RAR5 archive to the vulnerable Stage 01 `libarchive_fuzzer` reproduces the saved `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow` write in `parse_tables()`.

format.name: 524-byte RAR5 archive with a table-present compressed block whose Huffman-table RLE expansion overruns `bit_length[20]`
format.contract: The staged witness is a raw RAR5 archive. On the crashing path, `process_block()` parses a compressed-block header whose `block_flags.is_table_present` bit is set, then `parse_tables()` decodes the block's Huffman-table nibble stream. The trigger condition is an `ESCAPE` nibble (`15`) followed by a nonzero escape payload at a point where fewer than `value + 2` slots remain in local `bit_length[20]`; the vulnerable zero-fill loop then writes zeroes past the end of that stack array, matching the staged ASan `WRITE 7` in `parse_tables()`.
